title: Librarians Host "Avoiding AI" Workshops Amid Big Tech Backlash
body:
In a surprising turn of events, librarians across the United States have started hosting workshops that are gaining immense popularity, particularly among individuals who are frustrated with the pervasive influence of Big Tech in their daily lives. These "Avoiding AI" workshops, as they have come to be known, have been met with unprecedented demand, with many attendees eager to learn how to navigate the digital world without relying on artificial intelligence-powered tools. The phenomenon has highlighted a growing concern among the public about the role of technology in their lives and the need for a more balanced approach to its use.

At the heart of this movement are librarians, who have traditionally been seen as guardians of knowledge and information. By hosting these workshops, they are responding to a growing need among their communities for guidance on how to use technology in a more mindful and intentional way. The workshops themselves are often interactive and hands-on, with participants being encouraged to bring their smartphones and other devices to learn how to disable certain features and opt out of data collection. Librarians like Charlie Bailey, who has been leading these workshops in South Philadelphia, have reported being surprised by the level of engagement and interest among attendees, with many people expressing a sense of relief and empowerment at being able to take control of their digital lives.

The "Avoiding AI" workshops are also reflective of a broader cultural shift, in which people are beginning to question the impact of technology on their well-being and relationships. With the rise of social media and other digital platforms, many individuals have found themselves feeling overwhelmed and anxious, with some even experiencing symptoms of addiction. By providing a space for people to learn about the ways in which technology is shaping their lives, librarians are helping to facilitate a more nuanced and informed conversation about the role of tech in society. This, in turn, is contributing to a growing movement that seeks to promote healthier and more sustainable technology use.

One of the key factors driving the popularity of these workshops is the growing awareness among the public about the ways in which their personal data is being collected and used by tech companies. With high-profile scandals and breaches having highlighted the risks associated with data collection, many individuals are now seeking to take steps to protect their privacy and security online. The "Avoiding AI" workshops are responding to this need, providing participants with practical tips and strategies for minimizing their digital footprint and avoiding the most invasive forms of data collection. By empowering people with this knowledge, librarians are helping to promote a more equitable and just digital landscape.

As the demand for these workshops continues to grow, it is likely that we will see a proliferation of similar initiatives and programs in the months and years to come. This could have significant implications for the way in which we think about technology and its role in our lives, with a greater emphasis being placed on promoting digital literacy and critical thinking. By supporting and amplifying the work of librarians and other community leaders, we can help to create a more balanced and sustainable approach to technology use, one that prioritizes the needs and well-being of individuals and communities over the interests of Big Tech.

Looking to the future, it is clear that the "Avoiding AI" workshops are just the beginning of a much larger conversation about the impact of technology on our society. As we continue to navigate the complexities and challenges of the digital age, it is essential that we prioritize the development of a more nuanced and informed understanding of the role of tech in our lives. By supporting initiatives like these workshops and promoting a more critical and mindful approach to technology use, we can help to create a brighter and more sustainable future for all.
